subject: Capacity squeeze readout and actionable matrix — ClearCommerce reserved throughput gap
messages:
From: Tim Barker <tim.barker@clearcommerce.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearCommerce Ops <ops@clearcommerce.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden latency/error surge — urgent

Naomi,

We're seeing a big jump in tail latency and a bunch of 429/500 errors from the reserved capacity pool attached to our account (DC-4921). Impact started ~08:30 PT and affects both our inference and embedding routes; system-level throughput from our side has dropped ~40% compared to yesterday. Attached a CSV with representative request IDs and timestamps.

This is customer-facing — transaction flows are timing out for some merchants. Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood-side capacity issue or something in our integration? We need a triage plan + ETA to restore baseline throughput.

Tim
Director, Platform Engineering
ClearCommerce

Attachments: request_samples.csv
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tim Barker <tim.barker@clearcommerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency/error surge — urgent

Tim — thanks for the data. We're putting a bridge together now and triaging on two tracks: immediate customer-impact mitigations + root-cause diagnostics. Rishi, can you pull GPU utilization, queue-depths, and KV cache hit rates for ClearCommerce's pools (DC-4921)? Aditya, please review autoscaling throttles and any recent kernel/driver rollouts in the us-west fleet. Marissa, I'm looping you for comms and temporary commercial remediation if we need to offer credits.

Initial ask to the customer: can you confirm whether any model changes or request pattern shifts occurred on your side in the last 24 hours? If not, we'll assume this is on our side and prioritize restoration.

I'll send an initial impact summary within 60 minutes.

- Naomi
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: initial-impact-summary.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency/error surge — urgent

On Tue, Jul 12, 2027 at 9:23 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Naomi — thanks for the data. We're putting a bridge together now...

Quick triage notes (summary):
- Dedicated pool for DC-4921 reports sustained GPU utilization at 98–100% for the last 75 minutes.
- Queue depth for token-generation requests climbed 7x; KV cache hit rate dropped from 82% -> 58% (impacts long-chat reuse).
- Runtime telemetry shows frequent micro-GC pauses on one node (node-id: usw-gpu-73) likely due to a memory leak in the new attention-kernel path deployed 04:00 PT.

Short-term mitigations we can enact immediately (ETA shown):
1) Evict hotspot node (usw-gpu-73) and redistribute workloads: ETA 7–12 min (risk: transient token retries).
2) Temporarily route non-critical customer routes to a compatible hosted model (auto-fallback): ETA 12–25 min.
3) Increase batch-window for DC-4921 by 30% to improve throughput at the cost of slight median latency: ETA 10–20 min.
4) Enable quantized variant for heavy embedding routes (if customer's workload supports it): ETA 20–40 min.
5) Apply a runtime revert/patch for the offending kernel (requires rolling restart): ETA 2–3 hours.

We recommend 1+2+3 immediately to stop customer impact and 5 as the durable fix. I'll attach the GPU heatmap and queue traces.

- Rishi
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Attachments: runtime-gpu-heatmap.png
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency/error surge — urgent

Naomi — quick commercial note: ClearCommerce is a priority account (commit for Dedicated). They're already sensitive to outages given active merchant integrations. If we need to route them to hosted variants or reduce rate-limits, we'll likely need to offer a short-term credit and a weekly status cadence until baseline restored.

Also request: can we prepare a 1-page exec readout + action matrix for tomorrow's morning leadership sync? They want the short timeline of what we did, outstanding risks, and the ask (approve burst credits / prioritize patch). I can take the customer comms thread once we confirm the mitigation plan.

Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: EXEC READOUT: ClearCommerce capacity-squeeze — recommended decisions and timeline

Team / Execs (cc list above),

TL;DR — Dedicated pool saturation for ClearCommerce (DC-4921) was driven by a combination of a regressed attention kernel and an unusual burst in long-context chat traffic that reduced caching effectiveness. Immediate mitigations (eviction + host fallback + batch-window increase) restored ~85% of baseline throughput by 11:00 PT on 7/12. The kernel patch is ready and we can schedule a rolling restart to complete the fix.

Impact snapshot (peak):
- Throughput drop: ~40% at peak; now stabilized to ~6% below baseline after mitigations.
- Error rate (5xx/429): peak spike to 6.8% -> now ~0.9%.
- Customer exposure: merchant timeouts and increased support tickets — material risk to the renewal conversation.

Recommended decisions (asks for Exec approval):
1) Approve immediate consumption of 48 hours of cross-tenant burst credits for DC-4921 to provide additional headroom while patch completes. Estimated cost: incremental $18k.
2) Approve out-of-band emergency patch window tonight (rolling restart, 2–3 hours) to revert the regressed kernel path. Ops will do a canary and full roll; risk: transient retries.
3) Authorize a temporary commercial credit for ClearCommerce (propose 10% invoice credit for July) and two weeks of daily status emails + weekly calls.

Actionable matrix (owner / ETA / success metric):
- Evict hotspot node (Rishi): done 7/12 09:50 PT / success = queue depth < 1.5x baseline.
- Route non-critical traffic to hosted fallback (Aditya): done 7/12 10:05 PT / success = 80% of errorful requests resolved.
- Batch-window increase (Rishi): done 7/12 10:15 PT / success = throughput rise + lower CPU scheduling overhead.
- Kernel patch (Aditya/Rishi): ready / request exec approval for tonight / success = restored KV hit rates and stable GPU utilization < 85%.
- Commercial credit & comms (Marissa): need approval / success = customer satisfied + quieted escalation.

Docs and artifacts: exec-readout-onepager.pdf (attached), impact spreadsheet & logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-ClearCommerce-DC4921, ticket: JIRA: INF-8421.

Urgency: please approve items 1+2 within 4 hours so we can schedule the patch tonight. If you want a live 10-minute sync, I'm available at 14:00 PT.

- Naomi
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: exec-readout-onepager.pdf
